title: Case study: cutting sample loss from 18% to 4%
intro: How a small change in handling — and a very boring spreadsheet — halved the number of cores that never reached the lab.

add_special_note.heading: The problem
add_special_note.text: One core in five arrived unusable: cracked, contaminated or labelled with a code nobody could match to a plot. The loss was invisible in the field and obvious in the lab.

add_table.heading: Before and after
content_of_rows_separated_by_comma: Relabelling time per batch, 90 min, 10 min
Plots with a missing replicate, 11 of 36, 2 of 36

add_focus_list.heading: Three interventions
items_of_the_focus_list: A single pre-printed label sheet per plot, generated the night before.
Cores carried upright in a rigid tray rather than a soft bag.
A two-minute check at the vehicle before leaving each site.

add_content_to_page.add_paragraph: None of these required new instruments. The tray cost less than a replacement core; the labels cost a printer cartridge; the check cost two minutes per site.

add_quote.text: The cheapest improvement was admitting that the field is where data is lost, not the lab.
